title: Winter Vehicle Kit
description: Use this list before cold weather to add winter gear to your car kit and know what to do if snow or ice strands you.

items.text: Blankets or sleeping bags for everyone who rides in the car
Extra warm clothing: hats, gloves, wool socks, boots, and a heavy coat
Compact snow shovel to dig out the car and keep the tailpipe clear
Keep the gas tank near full - it gives you heat while stranded and helps prevent fuel-line freeze
Flashlight with spare batteries
Phone charger and a charged power bank kept warm inside your coat
Water in bottles that will not burst if frozen, and high-calorie non-perishable food
First aid kit
Jumper cables - cold weakens batteries
Sand or cat litter for traction
Ice scraper and snow brush
Tow rope or strap
Bright cloth or flag to tie to the antenna or door as a distress signal
Chemical hand and foot warmers
Winter-rated washer fluid and good wiper blades
Know the stranded rule: stay with the car unless a building is close and clearly visible - people get lost in blowing snow
Know the CO rule: clear snow from the tailpipe before running the engine, run it about 10 minutes each hour, and crack a downwind window
Turn on the dome light while the engine runs at night so rescuers can see you, and keep moving arms and legs
Check weather and road conditions before you leave, and tell someone your route and arrival time
Have tires, battery, antifreeze, and heater checked before winter
